Definition: A practical abstraction in which a piping system is represented by its connected centerline with components, supports, anchors, loads, and restraints attached to that line.
The primary global analysis model that maps the centerline idea to a connected line-element system with nodes and elements.
A point on the analytical centerline where elements, supports, loads, or components meet; carries explicit mechanical degrees of freedom.
A centerline segment or component representation between nodes that provides mechanics behavior (axial, torsional, bending, thermal, load, recovery).
An element-specific coordinate basis used to express element behavior and result recovery.
The common coordinate basis for assembly, supports, loads, displacements, reactions, and reporting.
A boundary condition or stiffness contribution that limits motion or adds a reaction path.
A stated mechanical loading basis such as weight, thermal change, pressure metadata, imposed displacement, or user-supplied loads.
A recovered force, moment, displacement, reaction, or mechanics stress component.
Translational and rotational freedoms carried by nodes in the frame model.
A separate user-data computation layer that maps mechanics results into user-defined categories and reports user-rule outcomes.

Notes: User-supplied input data with provenance, not a public default.

Definition: Mechanics-only recovery of stress components from open quantities and user-supplied section or pressure basis data.

Synonyms: local FEA handoff;local shell or solid model
Definition: A handoff path for local questions (nozzles, trunnions, lugs, branch details, attachments, specialty components, local load introduction) not well answered by a global centerline model alone.
Deterministic findings produced for incomplete models, invalid restraints, singular systems, nonconvergence, or unresolved assumptions.
Source attribution attached to user-supplied data, required for inputs and preserved across handoffs and reports.
Confirmation that the software solves the stated mechanics problem correctly within declared tolerances.
Separate validation families: frame mechanics, piping loads, stress recovery, nonlinear supports, rule packs, and reports.
